title: FontLab Blog
description: News, technical writing, and updates from FontLab.

items.title: FontLab Studio 5 and the Fontographer acquisition
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

2005 was a pivotal year for Fontlab Ltd. The company shipped FontLab Studio 5, which became the dominant professional font editor for the next decade. FontLab also acquired Fontographer from Macromedia, reviving a tool that had been dormant since the mid-1990s.

items.title: On fractional coordinates
items.content_html: Round a number too early and the error never leaves. That is the whole case for working in fractional coordinates while you design, and rounding to a grid only when you ship.

items.title: OpenType Layout feature classification
items.content_html: OpenType Layout features drive the correct display of complex scripts like Arabic and Indic, and they let users apply advanced typographic formatting. This is a classification of the registered feature tags, written for developers building UI to expose them.

items.title: All FontLab products run on macOS 10.9 Mavericks
items.content_html: FontLab tested its current product line against macOS 10.9 Mavericks. Everything passed.

items.title: TransType 4 for Mac and Windows
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

TransType 4 arrived in December 2013 as a complete rewrite of our font conversion app. It added multi-color OpenType output and web font export to its core toolkit.

items.title: FontLab Studio 5.2.1 for Windows
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab Studio 5.2.1 for Windows shipped in December 2013. It builds on the 5.2 foundation with new tools and hundreds of bug fixes.

items.title: Matthew Carter webinar
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

In February 2014, FontLab hosted a live webinar with Matthew Carter, a key figure in digital type design.

items.title: Brush Romans webinar with John Downer and Paul Herrera
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

On March 11, 2014, FontLab hosted a webinar on Roman capital letterforms and their origins in flat-brush writing. Sign painter and type designer John Downer presented alongside calligrapher Paul Herrera.

items.title: Color fonts: the next big thing? A FontLab tutorial
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Back in 2014, color fonts were a brand new frontier. This 103-minute tutorial with Adam Twardoch was one of the first deep dives into how to actually make them.

items.title: DTL OTMaster 5.0, vfb2ufo, and FontLab Pad 1.1
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

December 2014 brought a major update to DTL OTMaster, plus two new free tools. We released a command-line UFO converter and an updated color font typesetter.

items.title: Basics of Python scripting in FontLab Studio 5
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Automation unlocks the real power of a professional font editor. In this 70-minute tutorial, Adam Twardoch introduces Python scripting inside FontLab Studio 5.

items.title: How to space a font
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Spacing is where type design lives or dies. In this 53-minute tutorial, Thomas Phinney walks through sidebearings, optical principles, and the practical workflow inside FontLab Studio 5.

items.title: FontLab VI Public Preview 2 for Mac
items.content_html: FontLab VI Public Preview 2 (build 5844) is out for Mac, following the expiry of the first preview. We are still not calling it a beta.

items.title: New FontLab VI Public Preview for Mac
items.content_html: A new FontLab VI Public Preview for Mac is out, adding context menus, a Gallery panel for named shapes, faster glyph access, and italic-angle drawing.

items.title: FontLab's plans for OpenType 1.8 variable fonts
items.content_html: At the ATypI conference in Warsaw, Google, Microsoft, Apple, and Adobe jointly unveiled version 1.8 of the OpenType specification — and with it, variable fonts.

items.title: Free FontLab VI Public Preview for Windows
items.content_html: FontLab VI Public Preview is now available for Windows, alongside an updated Mac build. It is free until the final app ships.

items.title: FontLab VI ship update
items.content_html: FontLab VI will not ship in 2016 after all. The new target is February.

items.title: Deprecated vs. discontinued
items.content_html: “Discontinued” and “deprecated” sound like the same thing. At FontLab they mean two different fates for an old product, and the difference matters if you depend on one of them.

items.title: FontLab VI on macOS 10.9
items.content_html: Newer FontLab VI builds require macOS 10.10 Yosemite or later. Earlier Public Preview builds ran on 10.9 Mavericks; that support is ending.

items.title: What's up with VI @ FontLab?
items.content_html: A quick status report from the Public Preview period: FontLab VI was close to done, the bug list was short, and Variable Fonts were the last big feature going in.

items.title: FontLab Studio, TypeTool & old TransType on macOS 10.13 High Sierra
items.content_html: A compatibility note for owners of the older apps: FontLab Studio 5, TypeTool 3, and TransType Pro 3 had real problems on macOS 10.13 “High Sierra” and 10.14 “Mojave.” Here is what broke and what to do about it.

items.title: FontLab VI is here
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb }

FontLab Studio 5 was a workhorse. It shipped in 2004 and carried a generation of type designers through the OpenType transition. The app aged gracefully, right up until it didn’t. On 7 December 2017, we replaced it.

items.title: FontLab VI 6.0.9 update
items.content_html: FontLab VI 6.0.9, together with the previous 6.0.8 update, brought a batch of editing and export improvements. Both were free updates.

items.title: Free FontLab VI workshops at ATypI Antwerp
items.content_html: In September 2018, FontLab ran three free FontLab VI workshops at the ATypI Antwerp conference — two introductory sessions in the morning and an advanced one in the afternoon.

items.title: Font filters, components and glyph metrics in FontLab VI 6.1
items.content_html: FontLab VI 6.1 adds three things type designers had been asking for: real, standards-compliant components, a Font window sidebar that filters glyphs by script and category, and metrics expressions that link spacing across glyphs, layers and masters.

items.title: FontLab VI 6.1: components, sidebar filters, and metrics expressions
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab VI 6.1 arrived in October 2018. It added standards-compliant components, a Font window sidebar for glyph filtering, and linked metrics expressions.

items.title: DTL OTMaster 7.9 available now
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb}

DTL OTMaster 7.9 adds support for variable OpenType fonts. This includes the fvar, gvar, CFF2, STAT, HVAR, and MVAR tables. It includes a new Proofing Tool for printing and exporting PDF specimens, and a Side-by-Side Viewer that shows variation instances.

Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux. A full license is US$228. Upgrades from previous versions are US$57.

items.title: FontLab VI: 12 releases in 12 months
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

FontLab VI 6.1.2 shipped today. That made twelve updates in twelve months after the first public version of our new font editor.

items.title: FontLab VI 6.1.2: printing, Echo Text and the Tables panel
items.content_html: FontLab VI 6.1.2 adds printing, synchronized text across windows, a Tables panel for custom OpenType tables, and a faster Classes panel.

items.title: Design space axes and multiple masters in FontLab VI
items.content_html:
{.illu-thumb .illu-index}

Variable fonts force you to think in multiple dimensions at once. This four-minute video shows exactly how to set up a design space with axes and masters in FontLab VI. It gives you a concise, visual introduction to the core concepts behind variable font production.
